# 1 Enoch Chapter 96 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 96:1 — 'Be hopeful' vs. 'Have hope'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Be-hopeful, ye-righteous" | Literal; archaic 'ye' |
| LOGOS | "Have hope, you righteous" | Formal; natural imperative |
| PNEUMA | "Hold on, you righteous ones — have hope!" | Doubles the exhortation; adds 'Hold on' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'Have hope.' 'Be hopeful' (EMET) is passive; 'Have hope' is the correct imperative. PNEUMA's 'Hold on' is not present in the Ge'ez.

---

## 96:2 — 'coneys' vs. 'rock hyraxes'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "as-coneys before-the-unrighteous" | Traditional biblical term |
| LOGOS | "like coneys before the unrighteous" | Preserves traditional term |
| PNEUMA | "like rock hyraxes" | Zoologically precise modern term |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'coneys.' The Ge'ez shafan corresponds to the Hebrew shafan (Proverbs 30:26; Psalm 104:18). 'Coneys' is the established biblical rendering. 'Hyraxes' is scientifically accurate but breaks the biblical register.

---

## 96:2 — 'sirens' — translation of mysterious wailing creature

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-sirens-shall-wail over-you" | Preserves the unusual term |
| LOGOS | "the sirens wail over you" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "wailing creatures mourn over you" | 'Wailing creatures' avoids the mythological 'sirens' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'sirens.' The Ge'ez uses a term for a wailing or mourning creature; 'sirens' is the standard scholarly rendering from Charles onward. The textual tradition is uncertain here; retaining 'sirens' preserves the ambiguity rather than resolving it.

---

## 96:5 — 'finest wheat' vs. 'finest grain'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "finest-of-the-wheat" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "finest wheat" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "finest grain" | More general term |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'finest wheat.' The Ge'ez specifies wheat (hinta), not grain in general. Agricultural specificity matters in the context of economic exploitation.

---

## 96:6 — 'fountain of life'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "forsaken-the-fountain-of-life" | Literal; echoes Jeremiah 2:13 |
| LOGOS | "forsaken the fountain of life" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "abandoned the fountain of life" | 'Abandoned' for 'forsaken' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'forsaken.' The Ge'ez verb carries the covenantal weight of apostasy; 'forsaken' preserves this theological dimension better than 'abandoned.'

---

## 96:8 — eschatological reversal formula

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "many-and-good-days-shall-come to-the-righteous" | Literal Ge'ez compound |
| LOGOS | "many good days shall come to the righteous" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "the righteous will be living their best days" | Paraphrase; 'best days' is interpretive |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Many good days' preserves the literal Ge'ez. PNEUMA's 'best days' is interpretive and loses the quantitative dimension ('many').

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 6**
